item.title: Higashi Chaya District: Kanazawa's Best-Preserved Geisha Quarter — Guide
item.description: Higashi Chaya District is Kanazawa’s largest and best-preserved geisha entertainment quarter, its streets lined with distinctive wooden latticed teahouses (chaya) dating back to the early 19th century, some of which still operate as working teahouses hosting geisha performances today. Beyond its historic architecture, the district is now also known for shops selling Kanazawa’s famous gold leaf crafts and traditional sweets, many housed within the same beautifully preserved wooden buildings that once hosted the entertainment district’s original clientele.

item.title: Nishi Chaya & Kazuemachi: Kanazawa's Quieter Historic Districts — Guide
item.description: Nishi Chaya and neighbouring Kazuemachi are two of Kanazawa’s historic geisha districts, smaller and considerably quieter than the better-known Higashi Chaya across town, offering the same distinctive wooden latticed teahouse (chaya) architecture with far fewer crowds. Kazuemachi in particular sits along the Asano River, its narrow lantern-lit lanes and riverside setting giving it a particularly atmospheric feel, especially in the evening when the teahouse lanterns are lit. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kanazawa, Ishikawa Hours Streets always accessible; shop hours vary Admission Free to walk Time needed 45–90 min Best time Evening for lantern-lit atmosphere What to See Wooden latticed teahouse (chaya) architecture, quieter than Higashi Chaya.
